doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Why Bird became a focal point; Lennie Tristano
summary: Parker as a way to push jazz at KCR, Irv Schenkler, and Tristano yelling at Phil.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah that’s right in the little circle there. So you felt compelled to find out more about him?

Well if the angle we’re heading towards is why Bird, you know why does Charlie Parker become such a focal point in my career, I think I can explain that to you and I think it’s two parts. One is my discovering that he’s a good way to push jazz. Because you were mentioning a Hamilton College alumnus, Al Vollmer, he doesn’t like bebop but he likes Charlie Parker.

And the guys at KCR who I was trying to get them to like the music that Al Vollmer liked, they liked Ornette Coleman because they liked Charlie Parker. I said ahh, I see how that goes. So that’s part one. And then one of these people was a fellow named Irv Schenkler and he really produced the Charlie Parker festival on KCR because I really lit a fire for Bird. No he lit it himself, let’s give Irv Shenkler one hundred percent of the credit. But the Charlie Parker Festival is the turning point of KCR’s history. And that has a lot to do with Lennie Tristano. Because when Tristano — you see Tristano and I are great friends now that he’s been dead for a quarter century. When he was alive, I mean I think I was not only scared of him, I don’t think I liked him. Now I mean there are actually some doctoral theses that find us to be great friends and I guess we are, because I say so and he’s not here to say whether we’re not. But it was a very, very touchy situation that finally was resolved, the resentment I have of being yelled at by Lennie Tristano for basically the entirety of my adolescence and young adult life. Every day, yell. “Phil, you’re such a nice young boy. Why would you want to listen to Dexter Gordon when you can listen to Bird? I mean Dexter is totally derivative. Play more Bird. Listen to Bird.

Such a nice young fellow. Why waste your time?” And then I got on the radio and it got worse. “I never thought that you were stupid, Phil, I thought you were a beautiful cat. But that show you did today, Sonny Rollins. Play Bird.” And it’s a caricature now. I could do Lennie in voice thirty years ago. I mean and fool Lee Konitz. I did fool Lee.
